subject: Post-call: traffic peaks vs baseline & throughput sizing next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Ho <evelyn.ho@shipmate.ai>, ops@shipmate.ai
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: traffic peaks vs baseline & throughput sizing next steps

Hi Evelyn / Shipmate team —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the sizing run: 

Summary from our discussion
- Traffic shape: steady baseline ~80 QPS (chat endpoints) over 24h, expected daytime peak to ~420 QPS for ~20-30 min windows (user onboarding flows).
- Per-request token mix: average input 120 tokens, output 160 tokens; combined ~280 tokens per request.
- Streaming: yes for chat (token-by-token streaming required) with 95th pct latency target < 350ms server-side for single-stream responses.
- Concurrency: burst concurrency observed up to 600 concurrent open streams during onboarding spike.

Sizing ask / clarifying items we need from you (items 1-4 are blockers for a pilot estimate)
1) Can you share a 48h sample of traffic (timestamps + endpoint + avg tokens in/out per request)? A CSV is fine — see attached example.
2) Confirm what portion of calls must be streamed vs non-streaming (we heard ~75% streaming but want a %).
3) SLA tolerance for degradations during peak (e.g., allow graceful fallback to non-streaming for 5% of sessions?).
4) Any compliance constraints that would prevent us from enabling prefix caching or KV-cache reuse across sessions?

What Redwood will do next
- Run a throughput sizing baseline based on the sample you provide to produce two configs: (A) cost-optimized (aggressive batching, quantized model) for steady-state; (B) latency-optimized for peak and streaming.
- Provide recommended canary rollout: start with 10% of traffic on (B) for onboarding windows, auto-fallback to (A) if p95 latency > 450ms for N=5 mins.
- Schedule a smoke test (synthetic replay) to validate concurrency limits and streaming tls throughput — I propose Wed May 19 10:00 PT if that works.

Attachments: shipmate-traffic-sample.csv (template), redwood-slo-proposal.pdf (draft SLO mapping)

Next steps / asks for Evelyn
- Share the 48h sample and confirm streaming % by EOD Tue May 17.
- Let me know whether Wed 19 10:00 PT works for a 45-min replay + validation slot.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-8194

From: Evelyn Ho <evelyn.ho@shipmate.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, ops@shipmate.ai
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: traffic peaks vs baseline & throughput sizing next steps

Neha — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple quick clarifications below and attached is the 48h export (shipmate-48h-sample.csv).

- Streaming percent: 72% of chat open sessions are streaming. The remainder are single-request bot replies.
- We confirm per-request average tokens: input 110, output 170 (slightly different from call, sample has per-row counts).
- Degradation tolerance: We can tolerate fallback to non-streaming for up to 8% of sessions during the worst 10-minute windows, but prefer auto-fallback to be a last resort.
- Caching: we cannot share cross-customer KV caches; per-customer prefix caching is acceptable.

We can do Wed May 19 10:00 PT for the replay. Please include time for brief post-test sync.

--
Evelyn Ho
Head of Platform | Shipmate AI
evelyn.ho@shipmate.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Ho <evelyn.ho@shipmate.ai>, ops@shipmate.ai
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: traffic peaks vs baseline & throughput sizing next steps

Thanks Evelyn — helpful. A few internal notes / immediate asks from Redwood's sizing side: 

- We'll generate two 'target envelopes' using the numbers you sent:
  * Steady envelope: 80 QPS, 280 tokens/request (useful for cost profile)
  * Peak envelope: 420 QPS sustained for 30 minutes, 600 concurrent streams, 72% streaming at given token mix

- For the replay we need: a single signed service account token with read-only access to the sample replay bucket (we won't ship data off your VPC). Preferably rotateable credentials. Marcus to send a short IAM template.

- One technical caveat: streaming connections multiply TLS/session overhead — for 600 concurrent streams we'll need headroom for 800 TLS connections to absorb spikes. Please confirm your LB (nginx/ALB) supports that headroom or we can propose a small LB config change.

I'll run an initial cost/latency estimate and drop the PDF in the drive link before the Wed test. Priyom, can you draft the test plan (concurrency ramps + per-endpoint checks) and share by EOD today?

Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Performance | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Ho <evelyn.ho@shipmate.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, ops@shipmate.ai
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: traffic peaks vs baseline & throughput sizing next steps

On Mon, May 17, 2027 at 11:08 AM Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
> For the replay we need: a single signed service account token with read-only access to the sample replay bucket (we won't ship data off your VPC).

Thanks — noted. Evelyn, attaching the test plan (inline summary below). I kept the plan short to match the 45-min slot: 

Test plan summary (Wed May 19, 10:00 PT)
- 00:00-05:00 warmup: ramp from 10 QPS to steady 80 QPS (verify baseline latency).
- 05:00-20:00 peak phase A: ramp to 420 QPS over 5 minutes, hold 20 minutes, streaming ratio 72%. Validate p50/p95/p99 latency for streaming and non-streaming, and token throughput (tokens/sec).
- 20:00-30:00 cooldown: ramp down to 80 QPS. Check for KV-cache effectiveness when toggled on/off.
- Validation checks: p95 server-side latency < 350ms for streaming path (target), p95 non-streaming < 250ms, no more than 8% forced non-streaming fallbacks.

Deliverables after run: throughput heatmap (QPS vs tokens/sec), p95 latency by endpoint, concurrency connection table, and an immediate recommended config for canary.

Attachments: shipmate-replay-testplan.md (short); please send the service account info to ops@redwood.com and we'll confirm IAM.

Priyom Das
Performance Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
